_comment: Which machine is which, and what its results are worth.
ci.md section 2 says the two development laptops are the CI machines.
In practice there is also a third box that is neither: a laptop used for
writing code, where runs are mock. Without this registry a mock run on
it is indistinguishable in an archived bundle from a qualification run,
and that is precisely the confusion the evidence discipline exists to
role 'qualification' - the hardware in architecture.md section 2. Its
results are gate evidence and may be archived as such.
role 'development' - anything else. Runs are mock: they exercise the
harness, they never substantiate a claim. A T3 gate bundle produced
An unrecognised machine defaults to 'development'. Defaulting the other
way would let an unknown box quietly produce evidence.

machines.label: Profile L - RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, Core Ultra 9 185H, 32 GB
machines.runs: Host build, shader compile for both targets, CPU fixtures, cooker, Vulkan golden images, timing smoke. Cooking is Linux-only (D5), so this is the only machine that can produce content.

machines.label: Profile A - Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB unified
machines.runs: Host build, Metal golden images, timing smoke, decode of Linux-cooked packages. Profile A is not a qualification profile at R0 and is not gated; it becomes one from R2, one release behind on features (D2).

machines.label: Development laptop - Apple M2, 24 GB unified (Mac14,2)
machines.runs: Writing code, and mock runs that exercise the harness. This machine is NOT Profile A: it reports an M2 with 10 GPU cores and 24 GB against a claimed M3 Pro with 18 GB. Nothing measured here is a Profile A result, and no bundle produced here is gate evidence.
